title: stage-aware-shadow-rollouts-with-grace-window-and-lossy-sampling
author: Aisha Gomez
description:
Motivation: current shadow/canary primitives at Redwood route mirrored traffic with simple fixed sampling rates and immediate aggregation windows. This causes two operational problems in real product traffic: (1) bursty feature flags or short-lived user sessions produce noisy signals that trigger premature rollbacks, and (2) high-cardinality signals (e.g., per-customer QA tests) overwhelm the telemetry pipeline when mirrored at 100% for short windows.

This PR introduces a stage-aware shadow rollout mode with two cooperating mechanisms: a configurable grace window and loss-aware sampling. The grace window delays hard rollback decisions until a minimum sustained observation period has elapsed for the canary stage; during the window, transient anomalies are throttled by a hysteresis policy. Loss-aware sampling lets the orchestrator automatically lower mirror sampling on high-traffic routes or when a sampling budget is reached, while preserving representative coverage across customer segments via stratified reservoir sampling.

Changes include: deployment API additions for staged rollouts, runtime routing changes to support delayed decision timers, telemetry tags to mark grace-window samples, a lightweight reservoir sampler implemented in the routing layer, and aggregation logic in the rollout controller to compute sustained regressions (statistically significant degradations) rather than per-minute spikes. The description below includes a checklist, high-level commits, files changed, and review summary.

Checklist:
- [x] Add stage field to rollout spec (staged, shadow, canary, promoted)
- [x] Implement grace-window timer and hysteresis policy in rollout controller
- [x] Implement reservoir-based lossy mirror sampler in router (configurable by route and customer segment)
- [x] Tag mirror traces/metrics originating from grace window for downstream filtering
- [x] Add aggregation queries and alerting rule updates for sustained-regression detection
- [x] Unit + integration tests for sampler + controller interactions
- [x] Documentation updates (API + operations guide)

Context and risk: this is framework-level work for rollout safety. The sampler is intentionally conservative (defaults to 5% mirror) and off by default for managed-hosted tiers; Dedicated/Private customers can enable with explicit config. The aim is to reduce false-positive rollbacks while keeping observability signals useful.
commits: feat(rollout): add 'stage' enum to rollout spec and API surface
feat(router): reservoir sampler for lossy mirror sampling with stratification
feat(controller): grace window + hysteresis decision state machine
refactor(telemetry): tag mirror events with grace_window=true
docs(rollouts): operations guide for stage-aware shadowing
review_conversation: Kenji: Can you justify the default 5% mirror? Aisha: 5% is conservative and chosen to keep telemetry cost low; customers can opt up. Marta: How do we avoid biasing segment coverage when dynamic sampling reduces rate? Aisha: sampler is stratified by customer_segment and request_path and uses reservoir sampling to keep representation. Samir: Is the grace window tunable per rollout? Aisha: Yes, rollout.spec.grace_window_sec is per-rollout with org-level defaults. Kenji: CI flake on integration tests after the first push; looks like a race in sampler warmup. Aisha: Fixed by adding a deterministic seed and warmup hook in the second commit. Marta: Please add an ops playbook; approving after docs update. Final: approved by Kenji and Marta, Samir requested small telemetry naming fix which was addressed.
merge_outcome: merged by squash with release note prepended to changelog
release_notes: Add stage-aware shadow rollouts: grace window prevents premature rollback on transient anomalies
Introduce reservoir-based lossy mirror sampling to control telemetry costs for mirrored traffic
Operator notes: defaults conservative; Dedicated/Private users can tune sampling and grace windows via rollout spec
summary_line: Adds a stage-aware shadow/canary mode with a grace period and lossy stratified sampling to reduce noisy rollouts and telemetry costs while keeping statistically meaningful coverage.
